segments: 354. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
to the couriers bearing good news who were arriving,
and the heralds crying in the streets of Egypt:
"The Sultan has conquered,
and the Franks have been defeated!"
I ran to learn from the bearers of good news the manner of the victory.
And when I drew near,
I heard them saying:
"Rejoice and be glad,
for the Sultan is safe!"
And immediately I knew
that their good news was the reverse of their proclamation.
And in this year, when Sultan Qilij Arslan made peace with Manuel, king of the Greeks,
he came to Melitene,
and encamped against it for four months with a great army,
without stirring up war at all.
Instead, he commanded the troops,
and they built for themselves houses of mud bricks so that they might spend the winter,
and for him they also built large houses with stones that were on the graves.
Now the emir who was in it was of the family of Danishmand,
and he became afraid of his nobles,
lest, when pressed as if by hunger, they might surrender him.
He hastily sent to the Sultan,
and received a pledge for his life,
and he went out and crossed over to Hisn Ziyad {or: Zayd}.
And Qilij Arslan took control of Melitene from Wednesday, the twenty-fifth
of First Tishrin of the year one thousand four hundred and eighty-nine [1489]
of the Greeks [October 25, 1177 AD].
And in the year one thousand four hundred and ninety [1490]
of the Greeks [1178/1179 AD],
all the Franks agreed with King Baldwin,
and began to build a city on the banks of the Jordan,
in the place called Jacob's Ford,
so that by it they might pressure Damascus.
And Salah al-Din went out from Egypt and came against Baalbek,
because its governor had rebelled against him.
And when he pressed him in battle,
he received a pledge for his life,
and surrendered Baalbek to him.
And Salah al-Din was strengthened,
and entered the territory of Palestine.
And the Franks came against him and put him to flight,
and they took plunder from the territory of the Arabs and returned.
And while they were encamped, resting, and rejoicing as though they had conquered,
an ambush of the Arabs sprang upon them,
and they bound about a hundred warrior men from among the Franks,
and they also captured the Master of the Friars (Templars).
And Salah al-Din went against that place which the Franks had newly built and captured it.
Now there were five hundred friar brothers (Templars) in it.
